description: Coerce text to a string. Replace each character & < > " ' with its HTML named entity (& < > " '). Order matters: escape & first so the entities you write don't get re-escaped. Return the resulting string.
Match line against ^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$. If no match, return null. If match, return { level, text } where level is the count of # characters and text is the trailing text.
Match line against ^-\s+(.*)$. If no match, return null. If match, return the trailing text only (not wrapped in an object).
Return true if line starts with three backticks, false otherwise.

Take a raw text string. First HTML-escape it via the existing escapeHtml function (which is already imported into the module from elsewhere — assume escapeHtml is in scope). Then apply these substitutions in order on the escaped string: 1) **bold** -> bold; 2) *italic* -> italic; 3) `code` -> code; 4) [text](url) -> text. Use non-greedy or character-class regexes to avoid eating past the closing delimiter. Return the resulting string. Do not import escapeHtml; assume it is already a top-level function in this same module.

Split markdown by newlines into lines. Walk lines and emit block tokens. A token has shape { type, ...fields }. Skip blank lines (lines with only whitespace) entirely. If a line passes isFenceLine: collect all lines after it until the next fence line, join with '\n', emit { type: 'codeblock', text }. If parseHeading returns non-null: emit { type: 'heading', level, text }. If parseListItem returns non-null: emit { type: 'list-item', text }. Otherwise: collect contiguous non-blank non-special lines, join with a single space, emit { type: 'paragraph', text }. Return the array of tokens. Assume parseHeading, parseListItem, isFenceLine are already top-level functions in the same module.

Switch on token.type and return an HTML string. 'heading' -> parseInline(text) where N is token.level. 'paragraph' ->

parseInline(text)

. 'codeblock' -> 
escapeHtml(text)
(no parseInline; verbatim escape). 'list-item' ->
  • parseInline(text)
    • . Default -> empty string. Assume parseInline and escapeHtml are top-level functions in the same module.

Walk the tokens array. When you see a run of consecutive tokens with type 'list-item', collapse them into a single token of shape { type: 'list', items } where items is the array of those list-item tokens. Non-list tokens pass through unchanged. Return the new array.
